facts: Dynamic surfaces are cleared, terrain objects update, then the retained gMarioPlatform pointer is applied.
Non-terrain objects update and deactivated objects unload before update_mario_platform records the next pointer.
Y is assigned only inside the nonzero angular-velocity branch.
Object oVelY is not applied; only oVelX and oVelZ are added outside that branch.
A NULL retained pointer performs no displacement.
The behavior has no deletion, deactivation, respawn, or pointer mutation path.
The spinner is a persistent OBJ_LIST_SURFACE macro object.
Its loop only updates spinner rotation and loads its collision model.
Allocation zeros all 0x50 raw-data words, including face-angle and angular-velocity fields.
A reused slot therefore cannot inherit a prior platform's angular velocity.

retained_active_object_slots.interpretation: The 25-unit result is an ordinary collision snap onto the spinner's raised center ridge, not retained-platform displacement; every retained object had zero pitch/roll angular velocity.

analytic_bounds.derivation: For rigid rotation by theta, total point displacement is at most 2*r*sin(theta/2); vertical displacement cannot exceed total displacement.

required_chain: Mario stands within four units of a dynamic floor and gMarioPlatform records its object.
That exact object unloads after its surface remains available to find_floor.
A different terrain object allocates the same slot before the next frame's apply call.
The replacement has nonzero pitch or roll angular velocity and a sufficiently remote axis.
stale_pointer_assessment.incident_failure: The floor owner is persistent spinner slot 46. It neither unloads nor changes identity, and TTC_SPEED_STOPPED gives it zero pitch/roll angular velocity. The required chain cannot begin.
